Figure 1:Small action perturbations lead to distinct action effects.From the same initial state, actions drawn from a narrow distribution change the gripper’s approach only slightly, yet produce qualitatively different outcomes, where the cube is grasped, missed, or pushed away.
A faithful world model must reproduce how these outcomes shift as the action is perturbed, rather than only rendering a plausible video for generic actions.

Figure 2:Overview ofAFFECT.Frozen encodersϕ,ψ\phi,\psiextract video features from both the recorded and generated futures, and perturbation features from the logged action perturbations.
Pairing the centered perturbations with each set of video features gives the recorded and predicted action effects (Φ⁡(𝑶),Φ⁡(𝑶^)\Phi(\bm{O}),\Phi(\hat{\bm{O}})), which measure how visual change moves with the perturbation across rollouts.
TheAFFECTloss optimizes over the distance between the two distributions, so that generated futures respond to perturbations in the same direction and with the same strength as real ones.
Figure 4:Action-effect localization.Frozen-feature responses on UR5e relative to shuffled pairs, where brighter cells indicate stronger responses.

Figure 5:Open-loop long-horizon rollouts on UR5e in simulation.(a) Ground-truth rollout obtained by executing the action trajectory in the OGBench simulator.
(b, c) Videos generated by Cosmos3 and Cosmos3 +AFFECTwhen conditioned on the same action trajectory.
Frames are ordered in time from left to right.

Figure 6:Open-loop long-horizon rollouts on the real-world FR3.Each panel shows one episode.
(a) Ground-truth rollout recorded while the FR3 executes the action trajectory.
(b, c) Videos generated by Cosmos3 and Cosmos3 +AFFECTwhen conditioned on the same action trajectory.
Frames are ordered in time from left to right.
